FC-20.title: Figure C-20: Angle of Internal Friction vs. Relative Density (printed C-42, PDF 156)
FC-20.legend_hint: the open circles are the only symbols on this figure
FC-20.notes_for_reviewers: Angle of internal friction from direct shear tests (degrees) against relative density Dr for SS soil. The open circles are measured friction angles; two circles joined by a short horizontal line are one angle measured over a range of Dr, and each of the two circles counts as a symbol. The short horizontal joining lines are not curves. Circles at the edges can be cut by the frame. The solid curve runs through the middle; the two dashed curves run above and below it. On a dashed curve, a crosshair in a white gap between dashes is a no.

band-top.label: upper edge of the cross-hatched band

FC-21.notes_for_reviewers: Angle of internal friction from direct shear tests (degrees) against relative density Dr for LSM soil. Instead of curves the figure shows a cross-hatched band between two straight edge lines. The open circles are measured friction angles; two circles joined by a short horizontal line are one angle measured over a range of Dr, and each of the two circles counts as a symbol. The short horizontal joining lines are not curves. Circles at the edges can be cut by the frame. A row on the band asks about its upper or lower edge line; a crosshair on a hatching stroke inside the band but not on the named edge line is a no.

FC-23.title: Figure C-23: Angle of Internal Friction Versus Relative Density (From Direct Shear Test Results) (printed C-45/C-46, PDF 159)
FC-23.legend_hint: there are no symbols on this figure
FC-23.notes_for_reviewers: Angle of internal friction from direct shear tests (degrees) against relative density Dr for six soils, one curve each, named by the label printed beside it (RC2, PS, RS, RSM-b, RSM-a, SS). RC2 and SS are solid; the other four are dashed in different patterns. Between about Dr 0.4 and 1.0 the RS, PS and RSM-b curves cross and run close together: follow each one from its label. A crosshair on another curve, or in a white gap between dashes, is a no.
